title: Isaiah Chapter 56 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 56 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 56 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 56.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:1, what does the LORD command us to keep?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment and do justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:1 states, 'Keep ye judgment, and do justice' as commanded by the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD says that His salvation is near to come in Isaiah 56:1.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:1 says 'for my salvation is near to come,' confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: Who is described as blessed in Isaiah 56:2?
options: The man that keeps the Sabbath and does no evil
questions.correctAnswer: The man that keeps the Sabbath and does no evil
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:2 states, 'Blessed is the man... that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:3 says the son of the stranger who joins himself to the LORD is separated from His people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:3 specifically says, 'Neither let the son of the stranger... say, The LORD hath utterly separated me from his people,' meaning he should not say that.

questions.question: What does the eunuch say about himself in Isaiah 56:3?
options: Behold, I am a dry tree
questions.correctAnswer: Behold, I am a dry tree
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:3 records the eunuch saying, 'Behold, I am a dry tree.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:4, to whom does the LORD speak about keeping the Sabbaths and choosing pleasing things?
questions.correctAnswer: The eunuchs
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:4 says, 'For thus saith the LORD unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths...'

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 56:3, the son of the stranger who joins himself to the LORD is encouraged to despair because he is separated from God’s people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:3 tells the son of the stranger not to say that he is separated from God’s people, so he is not encouraged to despair.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to give the eunuchs who keep His Sabbaths in Isaiah 56:5?
options: A place and a name better than sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: A place and a name better than sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:5 states the LORD will give eunuchs 'a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 56:6, who are described as joining themselves to the LORD to serve Him and love His name?
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of the stranger
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:6 mentions 'the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the LORD, to serve him, and to love the name of the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:2 says that the son of man who layeth hold on judgment is blessed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:2 says, 'Blessed is the man... and the son of man that layeth hold on it,' referring to judgment and keeping the Sabbath.

questions.question: Which group is promised to be brought to the holy mountain and made joyful in the house of prayer according to Isaiah 56:7?
options: Those who keep the Sabbath and take hold of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Those who keep the Sabbath and take hold of the covenant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 says, 'Even them will I bring to my holy mountain... their burnt offerings and sacrifices shall be accepted.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 56:8, who does the LORD say He will gather besides Israel's outcasts?
options: Others beside those that are gathered
questions.correctAnswer: Others beside those that are gathered
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:8 states, 'Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 56, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Bring wine and fill yourselves with strong drink
questions.correctAnswer: Keep judgment and do justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:1 opens with the instruction to 'Keep ye judgment, and do justice,' which precedes other instructions.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:10 describes the watchmen as being alert and able to bark like dogs.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:10 says 'His watchmen are blind... they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down,' indicating they are not alert.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:11, what is the nature of the shepherds described?
options: They are greedy dogs looking only to their own gain
They are faithful and caring shepherds
They lead the flock to green pastures
They watch carefully through the night
questions.correctAnswer: They are greedy dogs looking only to their own gain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:11 describes them as 'greedy dogs which can never have enough... every one for his gain.'

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 56 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 56 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:5, what does the LORD promise to give to the eunuchs who keep His sabbaths and hold fast to His covenant?
options: A place and a name better than sons and daughters
A land flowing with milk and honey
A crown of gold and silver
questions.correctAnswer: A place and a name better than sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:5 states that the LORD will give eunuchs a place and a name better than sons and daughters, and an everlasting name that shall not be cut off, showing God's inclusive promise and honor for covenant keepers.

questions.question: What is the significance of keeping the Sabbath and holding fast to God's covenant according to Isaiah 56:6-7?
options: It leads to being brought to God's holy mountain and joy in His house of prayer
It guarantees riches and long life
It grants the ability to perform miracles
questions.correctAnswer: It leads to being brought to God's holy mountain and joy in His house of prayer
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:6-7 explains that those who keep the Sabbath from polluting it and hold fast to God's covenant will be brought to the holy mountain, made joyful in the house of prayer, and their sacrifices will be accepted, emphasizing faithfulness and worship.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 56:8 describe God’s attitude towards gathering people?
options: God gathers outcasts of Israel and will gather others besides them
God only gathers the descendants of Israel
God gathers people based on their wealth
God gathers only those who are priests
questions.correctAnswer: God gathers outcasts of Israel and will gather others besides them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:8 states that the LORD gathers the outcasts of Israel and promises to gather others besides those already gathered, highlighting God's inclusive plan to bring many to Himself.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:5 teach us about God's view of those who faithfully serve Him despite societal status?
options: God honors them with a better name than sons and daughters
God ignores their status and treats them the same
God requires them to conform to social norms
God only accepts their service if they have children
questions.correctAnswer: God honors them with a better name than sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:5 honors eunuchs who keep God's sabbaths by promising them a place and an everlasting name better than sons and daughters, showing God's value of faithfulness over social status.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 56:6-7, what can we understand about God's house and its purpose?
options: It is called a house of prayer for all people
It is a house only for Israel
It is a place for sacrifices exclusively
It is a fortress against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It is called a house of prayer for all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 declares God's house will be called a house of prayer for all people, showing God's desire for inclusive worship and prayer from all who serve Him.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:8 reveal about God's plan for the outcasts of Israel?
options: God gathers the outcasts and will gather others besides them
God leaves the outcasts to wander alone
God only gathers the outcasts during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: God gathers the outcasts and will gather others besides them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:8 highlights God's inclusive gathering, promising to bring in both Israel’s outcasts and others, reflecting His mercy and expansive plan.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 56:5-7 teach about the biblical virtue of faithfulness?
options: Faithfulness in keeping the Sabbath and covenant leads to honor and joyful worship
Faithfulness is only shown by material offerings
Faithfulness is irrelevant to God's acceptance
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness in keeping the Sabbath and covenant leads to honor and joyful worship
questions.explanation: Verses 5-7 connect faithfulness—keeping the Sabbath and covenant—with God’s promise of honor, a place in His house, and joyful worship, teaching the value of obedience and devotion.

questions.question: A believer feels excluded because of their background. Based on Isaiah 56:6-8, what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: God includes those who join themselves to Him and calls His house a house of prayer for all people
Only native Israelites are accepted by God
Exclusion is a sign of God’s disfavor
One must earn acceptance by works only
questions.correctAnswer: God includes those who join themselves to Him and calls His house a house of prayer for all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:6-8 reassures that God accepts all who join Him, including strangers, and welcomes all into His house of prayer, encouraging inclusivity and belonging.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:7, what will happen to the burnt offerings and sacrifices of those who keep the Sabbath and hold fast to the covenant?
options: They will be accepted upon God's altar
questions.correctAnswer: They will be accepted upon God's altar
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 promises acceptance of offerings from those who keep the Sabbath and hold to God's covenant, highlighting God's pleasure in faithful worship.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:5 teaches that those who keep the covenant will receive an everlasting name that shall not be cut off.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:5 specifically states that God will give an everlasting name to those who keep His covenant, which shall not be cut off, demonstrating God's eternal honor for the faithful.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:8 indicates that God will only gather the outcasts of Israel and no others.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:8 clearly says that besides gathering the outcasts of Israel, God will gather others as well, showing His inclusive plan beyond Israel alone.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:6 say about the sons of the stranger who join themselves to the LORD?
options: They serve Him, love His name, and keep the Sabbath without polluting it
They must offer gold and silver
They are not required to keep the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: They serve Him, love His name, and keep the Sabbath without polluting it
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:6 describes the sons of the stranger who join the LORD as those who serve Him, love His name, keep the Sabbath from polluting it, and hold fast to His covenant, emphasizing wholehearted devotion.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 56:7 connect worship and inclusiveness?
options: God’s house is called a house of prayer for all people
Only priests may enter the house of prayer
Worship is limited to one nation
Sacrifices must be hidden from outsiders
questions.correctAnswer: God’s house is called a house of prayer for all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 emphasizes that God’s house is a house of prayer for all people, indicating the inclusiveness of worship and God's invitation to all who seek Him.

questions.question: What promise in Isaiah 56:5-7 can encourage believers who feel spiritually marginalized?
options: God promises a place, a name, and acceptance in His house of prayer
They must isolate themselves to be accepted
They will not be recognized by God
They will only be accepted if they have children
questions.correctAnswer: God promises a place, a name, and acceptance in His house of prayer
questions.explanation: Verses 5-7 assure believers that God grants an honored place, an everlasting name, and joyful acceptance in His house of prayer, offering hope and belonging to those marginalized.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:6 teaches that serving God includes loving His name and being His servants.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:6 explicitly states that those who join themselves to the LORD do so to serve Him and love His name, highlighting the importance of love and service in faith.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 56 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 56.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:9, who are called to come and devour?
options: All ye beasts of the field and beasts in the forest
The eunuchs that keep the sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: All ye beasts of the field and beasts in the forest
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:9 explicitly calls all beasts of the field and forest to come to devour, symbolizing destructive forces.

questions.question: What is the condition of the watchmen described in Isaiah 56:10?
options: Blind, ignorant, dumb dogs that cannot bark
questions.correctAnswer: Blind, ignorant, dumb dogs that cannot bark
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:10 describes the watchmen as blind, ignorant, and dumb dogs that cannot bark, indicating their failure to protect and warn.

questions.question: In Isaiah 56:11, the shepherds are criticized for what behavior?
options: Looking to their own way for gain
questions.correctAnswer: Looking to their own way for gain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:11 condemns the shepherds for being greedy and only looking to their own gain, lacking true understanding.

questions.question: What invitation do the greedy dogs give in Isaiah 56:12?
options: Fetching wine and filling themselves with strong drink
questions.correctAnswer: Fetching wine and filling themselves with strong drink
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:12 quotes the greedy dogs inviting others to join them in drinking wine and strong drink, reflecting indulgence and complacency.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of unfaithful shepherds as in Isaiah 56:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 34:2-6
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:2-6 similarly condemns unfaithful shepherds who feed themselves and neglect the flock, paralleling Isaiah 56:11's criticism.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 56:10–11 to describe the watchmen and shepherds?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:10-11 uses metaphor by comparing watchmen and shepherds to blind, dumb, and greedy dogs to illustrate their failures.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'sabbath' (שַׁבָּת) imply in the context of Isaiah 56:2 and 56:6?
options: A day of rest and holiness
questions.correctAnswer: A day of rest and holiness
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 56:2 and 56:6, 'sabbath' refers to a sacred day of rest and holiness, emphasizing keeping it without pollution as a sign of covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:8 states that the LORD will gather only the outcasts of Israel and no others.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:8 clarifies that the LORD will gather not only the outcasts of Israel but also others besides those already gathered, indicating inclusion.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 56:1 emphasizes keeping judgment and doing justice because God's salvation is near.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:1 commands to keep judgment and do justice in light of the imminent revelation of God's salvation and righteousness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 56:7 describe the LORD’s house in relation to all people?
options: An house of prayer for all people
A place of sacrifice for kings
questions.correctAnswer: An house of prayer for all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 says the LORD’s house will be called a house of prayer for all people, highlighting its universal accessibility.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the inclusive theme of Isaiah 56:7 about God's house being for all people?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 21:13
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:13 quotes Jesus calling the temple a 'house of prayer for all nations', echoing Isaiah 56:7’s theme of inclusion.

questions.question: In Isaiah 56:5, what does the LORD promise to eunuchs who keep His sabbaths and take hold of His covenant?
options: A place and a name better than sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: A place and a name better than sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:5 promises eunuchs an everlasting name and a place in God's house better than natural offspring, signifying honor and inclusion.

questions.question: Which earlier Scripture theme does the promise in Isaiah 56:5 about an everlasting name fulfill?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 17:5, the covenant with Abraham
questions.explanation: The promise of an everlasting name in Isaiah 56:5 reflects and fulfills the covenantal blessings given to Abraham in Genesis 17:5, extending God's promise of legacy.

questions.question: What is the authorial intent behind the depiction of greedy dogs and blind watchmen in Isaiah 56:10-11?
options: To criticize corrupt leaders failing their duties
To praise the faithful servants of God
To describe literal animals attacking the land
To prophesy a future animal invasion
questions.correctAnswer: To criticize corrupt leaders failing their duties
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:10-11 uses imagery of dogs and watchmen metaphorically to criticize leaders who are greedy, ignorant, and neglectful of their responsibilities.

questions.question: Which cultural context best explains the imagery of 'dogs' used in Isaiah 56:10-11?
options: In ancient Near East, dogs symbolized unclean, scavenging animals
Dogs were revered as sacred animals
Dogs were used as sacrificial animals
questions.correctAnswer: In ancient Near East, dogs symbolized unclean, scavenging animals
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near Eastern context, dogs were often seen as unclean scavengers, which makes the metaphor in Isaiah 56:10-11 a strong condemnation of the leaders’ behavior.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 56 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 56 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the LORD command in Isaiah 56:1 regarding judgment and justice?
questions.correctAnswer: Keep judgment and do justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:1 states that the LORD commands His people to 'Keep ye judgment, and do justice', emphasizing the importance of righteousness in their actions.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 56:2, who is blessed?
options: The one who lays hold on the covenant
The one who has many possessions
The one who can speak eloquently
questions.correctAnswer: The one who lays hold on the covenant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:2 declares that 'Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the son of man that layeth hold on it', which highlights the blessedness of holding onto God's covenant.

questions.question: What assurance does the LORD give to eunuchs in Isaiah 56:4?
options: They will be cast out forever
They will receive a better name and place
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive a better name and place
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:4 states that the LORD will give eunuchs 'a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters', assuring them of His acceptance and honor.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:7 say about the house of the LORD?
options: It shall be a house of prayer for all people
It shall be a place of judgment
It shall be a place of wealth
It shall be a fortress for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be a house of prayer for all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 proclaims that 'mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people', indicating God's desire for inclusivity and worship among all nations.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about gathering the outcasts in Isaiah 56:8?
options: He will gather only the righteous
He will gather the outcasts of Israel and others
He will only gather the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: He will gather the outcasts of Israel and others
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:8 indicates that the LORD will gather 'the outcasts of Israel' and 'others' to Himself, reflecting His inclusive plan for salvation.

questions.question: What criticism does Isaiah 56:10 make about the watchmen?
questions.correctAnswer: They are blind and ignorant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:10 criticizes the watchmen, stating they 'are all blind: they are all ignorant', highlighting their failure to fulfill their roles as guardians of the people.

questions.question: In Isaiah 56:11, what behavior of the shepherds is described?
options: They seek the welfare of the flock
They lead the flock to green pastures
questions.correctAnswer: They are greedy and self-serving
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:11 describes the shepherds as 'greedy dogs which can never have enough', indicating their focus on personal gain rather than the well-being of the people.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:12 reveal about the attitude of the watchmen?
questions.correctAnswer: They are complacent and indulgent
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:12 depicts the watchmen as saying, 'I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink', reflecting their indulgent and careless attitude.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 56:5 connect to the concept of identity?
options: It offers an everlasting name to the faithful
questions.correctAnswer: It offers an everlasting name to the faithful
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:5 states that the LORD will give eunuchs 'an everlasting name', signifying a new identity rooted in faithfulness to God.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:6 state about those who join themselves to the LORD?
options: They will be separated from God
They will serve Him and love His name
questions.correctAnswer: They will serve Him and love His name
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:6 expresses that those who join themselves to the LORD will 'serve him, and to love the name of the LORD', highlighting their commitment to God.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:3 warn against for the son of the stranger?
options: He should boast of his strength
He should say he is separated from God's people
questions.correctAnswer: He should say he is separated from God's people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:3 warns that the son of the stranger should not say, 'The LORD hath utterly separated me from his people', indicating that God's acceptance extends to all.

questions.question: How can Isaiah 56:1-2 be synthesized to reflect on the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation requires strict adherence to the law
Salvation is near and requires justice
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is near and requires justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:1-2 together emphasize that God's salvation is near and that it is closely tied to justice and righteous living.

questions.question: What combined message do Isaiah 56:4 and 56:5 convey about God's covenant?
options: God honors all who keep His covenant
Covenant is only for the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: God honors all who keep His covenant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:4 and 56:5 together reveal that those who keep God's covenant, including eunuchs, will receive honor and blessings from Him.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:7 and 56:8 together imply about the inclusiveness of God's house?
options: It is only for the righteous
It is a prayer house for all people
It is for the wealthy only
questions.correctAnswer: It is a prayer house for all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:7 and 56:8 emphasize that God's house is a place of prayer for all people, indicating His inclusive nature in gathering worshippers.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 56:10-12 reveal about the leadership in Israel?
options: They are blind, greedy, and indulgent
They cannot be swayed by distractions
questions.correctAnswer: They are blind, greedy, and indulgent
questions.explanation: Isaiah 56:10-12 portrays the leaders as blind and greedy, indicating a failure in their role to guide the people towards righteousness.
